title: sl2-analyzer save export
description:
One FromSoftware .sl2 save, read into plain data: which game it is, what the machine ran it on (if the caller said), and one object per populated character slot. Produced by sl2-analyzer (https://github.com/darthdemono/sl2-analyzer).

The governing rule of this format is that ABSENCE IS MEANINGFUL. A field is present only when it was read from the save; a game that does not store something simply has no key for it, so a consumer can always tell "this game has no death counter" from "this character has died zero times". Nothing is filled in with a default, a zero, or a null to make the shape regular. Progress sections are FLOORS: they report what the save proves, never what it rules out.

schema_version.description: Semver for this document format. MINOR adds an optional field; MAJOR would break a reader that trusted the previous shape.

generated.description: When the export ran, UTC. Not a save timestamp.

source.description: The save file itself. Everything here is read from the file or decided by which game it turned out to be.

filename.description: Basename of the .sl2 that was read.

game.description: Game id. dsr = Dark Souls Remastered, ptde = Prepare to Die Edition.

support_tier.description: How far this build trusts itself for this save. 'full' is identity, stats, souls, inventory and progress; 'inventory' means the stat block failed to validate (an unrecognised patch or an edited save) and stats were dropped rather than printed wrong. The tier is per character too — see character.tier.

save_format_version.description: The save's own format version word (DSR 71, DS3 98, ER 220/251). Absent for DS2 and PtDE, which carry no such field. This is NOT the game patch.

game_patch.description: Elden Ring only: the version of the regulation the save carries, e.g. "1.16.0". No other game stores one.

environment.description: How the game was run — SUPPLIED BY THE CALLER, never read from the save, which cannot know any of it. Present only when metadata was passed. Any key is accepted; the ones below are simply the ones this schema names. A key given more than once on the command line arrives here as an array, in the order given.

source.description: Where the game came from: Steam, GOG, Epic, a disc, …

version.description: Game version as the player knows it, e.g. "1.15.2".

dlc.description: DLC installed. Repeat the flag per DLC to get an array.

launcher.description: What started the game: Steam, Heroic, Lutris, …

notes.description: Anything else worth recording about the run.

characters.description: One per populated slot. An empty array means the file parsed but held no characters.

metaValue.description: A caller-supplied value. A string, or an array of strings when the key was given more than once. Other JSON types pass through when supplied via a metadata file.

countedItem.description:
An item and how many are held: [name, quantity].

The quantity is NULL in Elden Ring, whose owned-item list comes from the GaItem array and carries no counts — null means "not read", not "none". It can also legitimately be 0: a Dark Souls II save stores a record whose count field really is zero, and that is reported rather than tidied away.

character.description: One character. Only `slot`, `game`, `tier`, `name` and `level` are always present; every other key appears only if this game stores it AND this save yielded it.

slot.description: 1-based slot number as shown in game.

game.description: Same id as source.game, repeated so a character object stands alone.

tier.description: This character's own tier. A single slot can degrade to 'inventory' while its siblings stay 'full' — an edited or unrecognised stat block drops stats for that slot rather than printing wrong ones.

level.description: Soul level (rune level in Elden Ring).

klass.description: Starting class. DS2 and DS1 only — DS3 and ER do not have a calibrated offset for it, so the key is absent rather than guessed.

ng_plus.description: Journey / New Game+ cycle; 0 is the first playthrough.

deaths.description: Death counter. DS1 and DS2 only; DS3 appears not to store one.

soul_memory.description: DS2 only: total souls ever earned.

embered.description: DS3 only. When true the max HP below already includes the ~30% ember bonus.

stats.description: Attributes, keyed by the game's own names (Vigor, Endurance, … / Mind and Arcane in Elden Ring). Absent entirely at inventory tier.

inv.description: Inventory by category (weapons, armors, rings, spells, bolts, upgrade, consumables, online, emotes, bosssouls, talismans, ashes). Which categories exist depends on the game.

key_items.description: Progression items: keys, tomes, coals, ashes.

boss_souls.description: Boss souls / remembrances still held. Each one is proof of a kill; a consumed one is invisible.

unknown_count.description: Items whose id is in the save but not in the name tables. Reported rather than hidden.

equipped_weapons.description: DS3 only, keyed by slot ("Right Hand", "Left Hand 2", …). Names carry infusion and +N.

equipped_armor.description: DS3 only: Head / Chest / Hands / Legs.

bosses.description: Bosses proven dead, keyed by boss name; the value lists WHY, which is the point — every entry is auditable. A floor, not a roster.

boss_total.description: How many bosses the game's own tables can NAME — the denominator for `bosses`. Not a claim about how many the game ships.

bosses_missing.description: Tracked bosses with no evidence yet. A boss whose soul was spent can sit here while being long dead.

bosses_available.description: DS3 only: missing bosses whose prerequisites are all dead and whose area already has a lit bonfire. From the game's fixed route, not from this save.

bonfires.description: DS2 only: the flat discovered-bonfire list. `bonfire_areas` is the grouped view of the same data.

bonfire_areas.description: Bonfires by area. EVERY area is listed, including untouched ones, so an area reading 0/6 is visible.

prefixItems.description: How many the area holds in total.

pickups.description: DS3 only: one-off world items picked up, by area, from that area's pickup flags. Only areas whose flag group has a DERIVED base appear — an absent area is untracked, not empty.

covenants.description: Covenants discovered, keyed by name; the value says what proves it. Distinct from the worn `covenant`.

questlines.description: DS3 only: one-off rewards obtained, keyed by the NPC or landmark that gives them.

cinders.description: DS3 only: Lords of Cinder whose cinders are confirmed placed on the throne by a mapped flag.

lords.description: DS3 only: the Lords of Cinder. There are exactly four, so this section has a real denominator.

placed.description: How many are on the throne, derived arithmetically as (lords defeated - cinder items still held) — which is why it can be known without every throne flag being mapped. NULL on NG+, where the thrones reset but the defeat flags do not, so the subtraction would over-report; there the `named` list from mapped flags is all there is.

dead.description: How many of the four are proven dead.

held.description: How many sets of Cinders of a Lord are still in the inventory, i.e. killed but not yet offered.

named.description: The lords whose placement a mapped throne flag confirms. Shorter than `placed` whenever a lord's flag is not pinned yet — three of the four are.
